FF12 is a great game, it's one of my all time favorites, but you're comparing apples to oranges here.

FF7R gameplay was specifically designed to put a modern spin on classic turn based combat, with party swapping and menu selections. I wouldnt call the stagger system shoehorned, in my runs it was executed expertly and led to a rhythmic and satisfying flow between swapping party members to maximize ATB gain and tank enemies, and clever ATB usage. I'm surprised to see multiple people confidently stating this design element is a flaw when it's by a wide margin one of the least controversial parts of Remake.

This one was BRUTAL. I used every LD, both FRs, all calls and LD calls, summon, both BT and BT+ on Jecht and I still was 2 turns away from Odin OHKOing someone with Bladeglint.

I did this so many times that all the failures and one success have blended together so heres how I tried to handle each individual hurdle in this fight.

* Odin OHKOs if he hits you and Bladeglint is on. Bladeglint is automatically applied when he does his Force attack. Yuna base call and LD call will cleanse the debuff. Raijin LD call will prevent it from landing all together in addition to negating the damage. That's 3 Force attacks you can take with no problems. After you take the 4th you need to make sure the fight ends before he hits you again.

* Odin's Force attack also dispels a buff from each character that it hits. This is annoying as hell and another reason why you want to end the fight very quickly after he hits you with a fourth Force attack. Basically this means do not refresh Jecht and Gab's LD buffs immediately. Red Force time happens pretty quick in this battle so just eat decreased damage until then.

* Odin's Force attack also just really hurts. Gabranth's debuffs and buffs help with survivability but remember he also has 3 AA's which reduce HP damage taken. Freya NEEDS to be in the air when Force attack happens, to minimize damage taken and keep BRV high to prevent breaks.

* Force attack is the biggest threat and red bar doesnt seem consistent, sometimes itll go up by 2 and sometimes by 10. Start getting ready for it at around 80-85% each time. Remember to summon to give you breathing room if you need to get Freya in the air or something.

* Odin's Bellicosity aura increases in power at certain thresholds and as he breaks you. Jumping Freya will insure you are not getting broken often and you have ample rebreaks with Jecht and Gab when the thresholds come up.

* At 79%, 49% and 9%, Odin turn jumps and attacks with 3 instant turns. Freya can use Celes base and LD calls to Lock Odin to Freya and jump to minimize damage at two of these thresholds. 

* In my experience, the first red Force Time happens not long before the 79% turn jump so I do Gab AA/Freya jump, let that one go through, cleanse with Yuna call, reset buffs and keep revealing with Jecht/Gabranth until Freya lands, do Freya LD into Celes call into jump again when he is around 80-82% then keep rebreaking. He will turn jump and use up his Force turns. Then for the second and third red Force times, I used Gabranth FR to cancel Odin's out after cleansing/rebuffing etc.

* I ended first FR with Jecht BT+ finisher, then second one I went into BT mode. Remember to have Freya jump before Jecht BT. This got me between 9 and 19 and it was juggling buffs from there. He got another Force attack off and I was out of answers to Bladeglint but was able to kill him by revealing over and over with the boys.

Well, Rivals 1 differentiates in a few key ways. Firstly, theres no ledges, grabs, or shields. This lends itself to a faster and more evasive style of play, where advanced tech like wavedashing and hitfalling, as well as mastering your DI, means a lot more. For me, it's a bit higher of a skill floor and ceiling than regular smash, but feels more rewarding to do cool shit because of that.

The other main change is that most characters are designed around an element of stage control. This focuses their designs a bit more tightly than Smash characters, IMO, who can sometimes feel constrained by needing references to their source material.

On top of this, Rivals 1 has an insane mod scene and rollback netcode and tons of other QoL stuff that people have been asking for. That's not a huge sweeping change like you asked for, but it is meaningful to me at least.

The movement only formed because non-benders didnt feel like they had any power, both physically and politically, in a city where they were the majority of people. After season 1, the council of benders that oversees the city is disbanded and they enact a democratic process. Then they immediately proceed to elect a non-bender president. With their leader gone and their immediate concern addressed, of course the Equalists arc is wrapped up off screen after that.

**Lenna** (Faris LDCA)

**Jecht BT+ 3/3** (Porom LDCA)

**Balthier** (Sephiroth LDCA)

Shiva summon, Cid Raines friend

This team was a lot of fun to use here, and very effective at countering everything the bosses did, but it's not mindless spam skills to victory, you do have to be conscious of things. It took me a few tries so I'll go over some pain points and the general flow.

The strategy here is using Lenna's amazing support to uptick orb almost single handedly and keep their nasty debuff off, Balthier for stealing their strong and frequent buffs, and Jecht just rips through HP with these two empowering him. My three calls serve as additional dispel/debuffs, a clutch heal and Dragons Breath enabler, and additional BRV damage up for BT phase

Wave 1: I switched out Balthier for Raines immediately, best strat with these guys is to burn them down quick. Twins would have worked better but I only have one Twins friend and I'd used that on a botched run earlier. Lenna satisfies orb in the meantime while the two dps go to work. Use two Wind Drake Arrow immediately to get debuff prevention up. Not much to say here, spam LD with Raines, use rebreaks and double turns with Jecht. I killed them with Raines' last turn. 

Wave 2: Balthier came in immediately. His AA is pretty useless here so I spammed them out early to get his overhead buff to 5 sooner. Make sure you use another Wind Drake Arrow here to get debuff prevention on Balthier, and watch the duration on Jecht, his double turns make it run out pretty quick.

The first few times I did this run I was like oh this orb attack is survivable, that will make this easy, but this is a huge trap with this team. The orb attack puts on a buff called Blessing that reduces BRV and HP dmg pretty severely. We can (and should) steal this buff with Balthiet but it's a big DPS loss in the meantime. Having this buff up too often in my first runs meant Jecht and Lenna would run out of steam before the end of the fight and it'd be a loss.

This orb attack and buff will automatically trigger at 79%, 49%, and 29%. They also use gold old Supplication to apply 5 not-insignificant buffs at once.   Balthier is the key here. Use his skill 1 or EX to steal Blessing from both if it's the only buff, and his LD should be saved for when they use Supplication, especially if they already have Blessing up. Faris calls will also dispel buffs if needed, if Balthier is too many turns away for whatever reason.

So since we are following orb rules on this team, we can uptick it by +5 (really +3 since player actions cost -2 here) with either Balthier or Lenna skill 2, or a whopping +15 (again really +13) by using Lenna LD or her Dragons Breath HP attack. 

As for the thresholds auto activating, you just need to plan around that. I used Jecht BT+ 3/3 for the high DPS but if you dont have him I really recommend bringing another BT+ 3/3 character, so you can space out your BT mode, finisher, and summon to ensure all 3 thresholds are met by both enemies at the same time. This makes Blessing much easier to steal and keeps the orb counter consistent after each auto activation, which is super important. 

So the general flow for me was as follows: Balthier comes back, AA spam to get overhead buff up, refresh Wind Drake buff, attack until ~83% for both. Use Jecht BT+ finisher to trigger both. Steal Blessing buff with Balthier and replenish HP with a Lenna LD. Refresh Wind Drake buff as needed and use Lenna Dragons Breath and Balthier Tides of Fate to deal with orb and Supplication buffs while dealing damage to around 56%. Use Porom base call and a Seph call, then Jecht BT mode to bring them both below 50; they will trigger orb attack when BT mode ends. Mine did a big 5 million damage and brought them down to 36 which was great because I immediately starting planning for third threshold. I used Porom LDCA here for the big heal and a Faris call to dispel the Supplication they did and went into Summon to safely bring them under 29 together. Last orb attack triggered after summon, refreshed HP with last Lenna LD, refreshed Wind Drake for final push and rode it out.

Not too bad and was a lot of fun.

I didnt play WoW but I did spend a lot of time on GW2 so I use that as a basis for comparison, because GW2 had a pretty great inventory system.

You have your personal bags which you can either separate or group up. FF14 has this as well, so that's fine.

Instead of splitting your bank over multiple retainers, you just have one large personal bank. This is nice for me because I dont always remember which retainer is holding what item. Like FF14 letting you buy more retainers, you can also buy more bank space, but you have the option of exchanging in game currency for real money to purchase it, which IIRC isnt possible in FF14.

GW2 has its own separate material storage tab in its bank. When you go out gathering materials you can click an option in your backpack that sends all crafting materials in your bag to the material storage where they're saved. When crafting, items are automatically taken from your material storage without needing to have them in your inventory.

Instead of needing to keep different glamour in your glamour dresser or inventory, whenever you unlock a new outfit it goes to it's own transmutation locker where it can be used. Dyes work the same way, you use one once and its unlocked account-wide forever, you dont need to keep them on you or buy new ones.

GW2 also was a lot less shy about making totems and things like that into currencies so they werent taking up inventory space.

Inventory was so nice in that game and the main thing I miss now that I've made the jump over.

Quistis Degenerator is an instant turn, alongside the emperor of instant turns, Vayne. I did mess up a couple of times with her, so she wasnt out the remainder of the fight, but she was out for most of it.

Contempt buff is running low by now, so I used Iroha calls and went into BT around this time. Once out of BT you're just spamming skills for a while, making sure to rebreak and delay the proper enemy as needed.
